parameters.content:
## Track Walmart prices and split deals from marketplace offers

No price tracker subscription and no retailer API approval. Every week this searches Walmart for the products you care about, then **routes the rows three ways**: a full price history gets everything, a deals tab gets only the items with an advertised price cut, and a marketplace tab gets the offers that are not sold by Walmart itself.

Rows are keyed by Walmart's own item ID, so the same item at two prices in two different weeks is a price change you can read straight off the sheet without a formula.

**Who's it for**
Resellers and buyers watching a shortlist, brands checking what their own products sell for, and anyone who wants to know when a price moves without refreshing a tab.

**How it works**
1. A schedule trigger fires once a week
2. One Set node holds the searches you track
3. The Apify node searches Walmart for each one
4. A Code node keys each row by item ID and works out the discount
5. A Switch sends price cuts and third party offers to their own tabs

**Setup**
1. Create a free Apify account and add your API token to the Apify credential
2. Connect your Google account in the Sheets nodes and pick a spreadsheet
3. Replace the example search with your own products

**Make it yours**
Three optional nodes sit unconnected at the bottom of the canvas. Drag a connection from the **Price cut** output into any of them to filter to deep discounts only, post to Slack, or POST the row to your own endpoint.

**Good to know**
Search mode never reported an out of stock item over 60 rows across four different searches, so no stock column is mapped rather than shipping one that is always empty. Sponsored rows are ads and are marked as such, so exclude them before reading rank as organic.
Actor: https://apify.com/johnvc/walmart-api?fpr=9n7kx3&fp_sid=n8n

### 1. Schedule
Runs every Monday morning. Change the cadence, or swap in a manual trigger while you test.

### 2. Your input
The searches to track and how many results to take from each. This is the only node you edit.

### 3. Fan out
Turns your search list into one Walmart search each.

### 4. Fetch
Runs the Walmart API actor in search mode. Add your Apify credential here.

### 5. Clean
Keeps only real product rows, so an upstream error never reaches the sheet.

### 6. Shape
One row per product, keyed by Walmart's item ID, with the advertised discount worked out as a percentage.

### 7. Route
One row can leave by more than one output: an item that is discounted **and** sold by a third party lands on both tabs. The history below gets every row regardless.

### 8. Deliver
Three tabs in one spreadsheet: deals, marketplace offers, and the full history. Columns map automatically.

### Price history is a sheet diff
Every run appends a dated snapshot keyed by item ID. The same item at two prices in two weeks is a price change, and the Was price column catches a cut the same week Walmart advertises it.

### Sponsored rows are ads
Across 60 measured rows, 35 were sponsored placements. Their rank is paid, not organic, so filter the Sponsored column out before you read Rank as a ranking. The same item can also appear twice, once sponsored and once organic.

### Who is actually selling it
Only about two thirds of results are sold by Walmart itself. The rest come from marketplace sellers, where the price is not comparable and returns work differently. That is why they get their own tab instead of being mixed into the history.

### Prefer a dedicated node?
There is a community node for this actor: `n8n-nodes-walmart-api`. Install it from Settings then Community nodes if you would rather configure Walmart with typed fields than a JSON body. This template uses the official verified Apify node so it runs on n8n Cloud with nothing to install.

## Optional add-ons, not wired up

These three are deliberately left unconnected. Pick what fits, drag a connection into it from the **Price cut** output of **Route by what matters**, and delete the rest.

**Only deep discounts** drops anything under a 20 percent cut, so a one dollar move does not page anyone. **Slack** posts the deal into a channel. **HTTP Request** POSTs the row to any endpoint you own, which is the escape hatch if your alerting lives somewhere else. Slack needs its own credential before it will run.
